## Not Just at Rest

<!-- STEP id="not-equilibrium" -->
The system isn't in equilibrium anymore.

Apply Newton's second law to the box and its pulley, treated as one system of mass $M$.

<!-- STEP id="2t-minus-w" -->
## Two Segments, Not One

Two segments still pull up, each with tension $T$ — together that's $2T$.

$$2T - W = Ma$$

<!-- STEP id="worked-example" -->
## A Worked Example

An 8 kg box, weight 78.4 N, pulled with $T = 50$ N:

$$a = \frac{2(50) - 78.4}{8} = \frac{21.6}{8} = 2.7 \text{ m/s}^2$$

<!-- STEP id="same-law-doubled" -->
## Same Law, Doubled Force

**Pull harder than half the weight, and the box accelerates upward — same second law, just with $2T$ instead of $T$.**
